Morbstack guest filesystem/networking tool apk provenance
============================================================

Source repo: https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.24/main/aarch64/
Index:       APKINDEX.tar.gz from that same directory (fetched over HTTPS,
             used only to resolve exact version/release + the transitive
             `so:`-dependency closure below; not shipped).

Purpose: give the guest mkfs.btrfs / mkfs.ext4 (for formatting /dev/vda on
first boot, see the persistence design) and legacy iptables/ip6tables (so
dockerd can program bridge NAT). Requested roots were `btrfs-progs`,
`e2fsprogs`, and `iptables`/`ip6tables`; the actual package set below is
the full transitive `so:` dependency closure of those roots (minus `musl`
and `zlib`, which are already present in dist/rootfs/alpine-minirootfs.tar.gz
as /lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1 and /usr/lib/libz.so.1.3.2 respectively —
confirmed by inspecting that tarball directly, not assumed).

iptables note: Alpine 3.24's plain `iptables` apk is the nft-backed
variant — its `D:` line pulls in so:libnftnl.so.11 and so:libmnl.so.0, and
its `p:` (provides) line only advertises cmd:iptables-nft*, cmd:ip6tables-nft*
etc, NOT a plain `iptables`/`ip6tables` command. Per task instructions
("prefer the legacy binaries... avoids needing nft userspace"), this repo
instead fetches `iptables-legacy`, which depends on so:libip4tc.so.2 /
so:libip6tc.so.2 (the classic xtables-legacy libiptc, not libnftnl) and
ships a single `xtables-legacy-multi` busybox-style multi-call binary at
usr/sbin/xtables-legacy-multi, symlinked *only* as:
  usr/sbin/iptables-legacy, usr/sbin/iptables-legacy-restore,
  usr/sbin/iptables-legacy-save, usr/sbin/ip6tables-legacy(-restore|-save),
  usr/bin/iptables-xml
i.e. it does NOT ship anything literally named `iptables` or `ip6tables`
(that naming is reserved for the nft package's alternatives system, which
we don't install). scripts/mkinitramfs.sh therefore creates the plain
names itself as symlinks -> xtables-legacy-multi when staging the
initramfs (see the "iptables-legacy" section of that script) so dockerd
(which execs a program literally named "iptables"/"ip6tables" on PATH)
finds the legacy implementation.

iptables note, part 2 (added after live testing): the plain `iptables`
apk IS fetched after all, but only as the carrier for one directory —
usr/lib/xtables/. That directory holds the 112 match/target extension
modules (libxt_addrtype.so, libxt_MASQUERADE.so, libxt_conntrack.so,
libxt_comment.so, libxt_multiport.so, ...) that libxtables dlopen()s at
rule-parse time, and Alpine ships them in the main package and nowhere
else. The legacy frontend needs them exactly as much as the nft one does:
they are backend-agnostic, and their entire DT_NEEDED closure is
{libc.musl-aarch64.so.1, libxtables.so.12} — both already present — so
taking them adds no new dependency and does not reopen the nft question.
scripts/mkinitramfs.sh stages `./usr/lib/xtables` out of this apk and
drops its usr/sbin on the floor; that usr/sbin is the nft frontend
(xtables-nft-multi, needing libnftnl/libmnl, which we still do not ship)
and would additionally clobber the iptables/ip6tables symlinks described
above. Shipping iptables-legacy without these modules was a shell with no
ammunition: `iptables` resolved on PATH, then dockerd died on its very
first NAT rule with

  iptables v1.8.13 (legacy): Couldn't load match `addrtype':
  No such file or directory

leaving dockerd in a crash-restart loop and the whole engine unusable.
Found by running the functional gate ladder against a real VM.

Verification: each apk was downloaded once over HTTPS from
dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org and its sha256 recorded below at fetch time
(archive-hash-pinned for future reproducibility/tamper-detection), the
same approach dist/guest-bin/PROVENANCE.txt uses for the Docker static
binaries — Alpine does not publish a per-apk detached checksum sidecar
the way it does for the minirootfs tarball (dist/rootfs/PROVENANCE.txt),
and the in-index `C:` checksum uses apk-tools' own hashing convention
(sha1 over the control+data tar streams, excluding the signature stream)
rather than a plain whole-file digest, so it is not directly comparable
to `sha256sum <file>` and was not used here.

Cached under dist/apks/ (fetched once, re-fetched by
scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh --fsutils-only only if a cached file's
hash no longer matches).

  zstd-libs           1.5.7-r2   main  2bb5136c89f5b0bbe1554c8915a3b520d5aa63ae2a51d4d821eb81698db5a818  libzstd.so.1 (btrfs-progs dep)

Explicitly NOT fetched (already present in dist/rootfs/alpine-minirootfs.tar.gz):
  musl   1.2.6-r2  -> /lib/libc.musl-aarch64.so.1, /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1
  zlib   1.3.2-r0  -> /usr/lib/libz.so.1.3.2 (version matches exactly)

Each .apk is a concatenation of gzip streams (signature.tar.gz +
control.tar.gz + data.tar.gz per the apk v2 format); a plain `tar xzf`
transparently decompresses all of them and interleaves their members,
which is all scripts/mkinitramfs.sh needs — it extracts each apk into a
scratch dir and copies over everything except `.PKGINFO` and `.SIGN.*`
(the control-tar metadata/signature files, not part of the installed
package).

Fetched by scripts/fetch-guest-assets.sh (--fsutils-only).
